G0235.as:
ἀλλά (ἀλλ’ usually bef. α and υ, often bef. ε and η, rarely bef. ο and ω, never bef. ι; Tdf., Pr., 93 f.; WH, App., 146), adversative particle,
stronger than δέ; prop. neuter pl. of ἄλλος, used adverbially, with changed accent; hence prop. otherwise, on the other hand (cf. );
1. opposing a previous negation, but: οὐ (μὴ) . . . ἀ., , , , al.; rhetorically subordinating but not entirely negativing what precedes, οὐ . . . ἀ., not so much . . . as, , , , al.; with ellipse of the negation, , , 7:7, , , al.; in opposition to a foregoing pos. sentence, ἀ. οὐ, , ; οὐ μόνον . . . ἀ. καί, , , al.; elliptically, after a negation, ἀ. ἵνα, , , al.; = εἰ μή (Bl., §77, 13; M, Pr., 241; but cf. WM, §iii, 10), , .
2. Without previous negation, to express opposition, interruption, transition, etc., but: , ; before commands or requests, , , , al.; to introduce an accessory idea, ; in the apodosis after a condition or concession with εἰ, ἐάν, εἴπερ, yet, still, at least, , , , , al.; after μέν, , , ; giving emphasis to the following clause, ἀλλ’ ἔρχεται ὥρα, yea, etc., ; so with neg., ἀλλ’ οὐδέ, nay, nor yet, .
3. Joined with other particles (a practice which increases in late writers; Simcox, LNT, 166), ἀ. γε, yet at least, , ; ἄ ἤ., save only, except, , ; ἀ. μὲν οὖν, (on this usage, v. MM, VGT, s.v.).
